text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic visits Ghana and arrives in Guinea as part of his African tour.
- Turkish parliamentary delegation due to visit Belgrade on Monday, the first since breakup of the former Yugoslavia.
- McDonald's plans to have 13 restaurants in Yugoslavia in 1997, 21 in 1998 and 60 by the end of the century, says the acting director for Mcdonald's Yugoslavia Branimir Lalic.

- Plants of the Serbian Oil Refinery (NIS) are now working with 60 percent capacity and are ready to start developing after five years of blockade, says director of NIS Pancevo refinery Radovan Pesikan.

- Slovenia actually owes Yugoslavia two billion dinars ($400 million), says director of the Beogradska Banka Nicosia branch Borka Vucic. Slovenia has asked for freezing of former Yugoslav national bank's assets in Beogradska banka.
- The dispute over the Prevlaka peninsula can be resolved through negotiations, says Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic.
- Real investments in Yugoslavia can be expected only after regulation of relations with the IMF, says director of Societe Generale in Belgrade Dragisa Lekic.
- If Yugoslavia does not abolish visa fees for entry into Yugoslavia the Sarajevo-Belgrade bus will stop operating, says Bosnian transport ministry.
- Office building with 7,000 square metres for firm Progres opened in central Belgrade on Sunday by mayor Nebojisa Covic, Serbian parliament Speaker Dragan Tomic and other top officials.
- Yugoslav economic delegation, headed by president of Yugoslav chamber of commerce and minister without portfolio Vuk Ognjenovic is visiting France.
- Yugoslav Aviogenex plane was held up at Zurich airport over outstanding debt of 700,000 German marks to Credit Lyonnais of France.
- Shipbuilder Sava from Macvanska Mitrovica concludes deal to build two vessels worth 23 million German marks for Dutch corporation Damen.
- Rehauling of hydroelectric power plant Djerdap II will be completed by end of October and the plant will be ready to start production in November. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 43 05
